source: D1 waba-worker: ProductItem + KypGuide (required + active only)

requiredQuestions.question: Confirm it is genuinely the 'big' size vs the standard triangle cleaner
Ask trim: with brush or with studs, and brush type if applicable
Confirm size -- many clients order this by colour name alone ('Blue Cleaner'), so size still needs confirming
Ask quantity
Offer a reference picture if unsure
Ask quantity in pieces -- one size only, no size question needed
Ask ply/grade: 2 ply (Indian manufacture), 4 ply (imported, sturdier), 6 ply light green (70% cotton / 30% polyester), or 6 ply dark green (100% cotton, best quality)
Ask quantity
Offer a reference picture if unsure -- a common market size is roughly 75x58x8 mm sold about 500 pieces to a carton, but confirm the exact size and pack count before quoting
Ask opening size: 8 mm, 10 mm, or 12 mm
Ask quantity
Ask which type: Namda tape, cotton tape (Nivard), or glue-backed (peel-paper) tape -- construction and MOQ differ by type
Namda tape: ask width and thickness; MOQ 100 m per roll
Nivard (cotton) tape: thickness is fixed at 1 mm, so only ask width; MOQ 50 m per roll
Glue-type tape: only available in 3 mm thickness; ask width and quantity; MOQ 100 m per roll
Always confirm quantity in meters
Ask diameter/thickness, length, and quantity
Request a picture to confirm the material -- fiber and nylon look near-identical and clients are often unsure which they actually have
Ask quantity and any brand preference -- Kangaroo and Max are the common manual brands stocked
If unsure, offer a reference picture
Ask grade and the number within the grade -- 4 grade families exist: GG (6 GG to 74 GG), XXX (3 XXX to 17 XXX), MF (3 MF to 13 MF), N / double-X (3 N to 25 N)
Ask fabric family: standard sieving fabric, Milling Forte (heavier thread, same opening, longer life), or heavy-duty XXX grade -- trade-off is service life vs open (sifting) area
Ask width: 3 standard widths stocked -- 115 cm, 136 cm, 158 cm
Ask length in meters -- priced and ordered per meter
Ask the plansifter make -- frame/stretching sizes differ by machine (1250x1250 mm and 1500x1500 mm are common)

Ask the micron opening if the client knows it; if not, ask what flour it is sifting (maida, suji/rava, chokar/bran) so the opening can be matched to the product, since spec is really driven by micron opening rather than the grade number alone
If the client is unsure of the grade, request a picture or a physical swatch of the old cloth
Ask the plansifter make -- three standard sizes/numbers (Type 1/2/3) exist and fit differs by machine; ask which type, or the diameter in mm, if the client is unsure
Ask material: rubber, nylon (= plastic), or PVC (clear, also called penny ball); PVC is also available in a food-grade variant
Ask material/hardness of the rubber if known
Ask quantity -- MOQ differs by material: rubber 500 pcs, nylon 200 pcs, PVC 200 pcs; order strictly in multiples of the MOQ
Offer a reference picture -- the three types look alike at a glance
Ask width: 1 inch, 1.5 inch, or 2 inch
Ask number of bales -- 1 inch = 30 rolls x 25 m per bale; 1.5 inch = 20 rolls x 25 m per bale; 2 inch = 15 rolls x 25 m per bale
Ask brand of the plansifter
Ask size of the channel
Ask quantity
Request a picture to confirm
Ask diameter and length in inches, being clear whether it is flat diameter or actual (inflated) diameter -- these two numbers are different and easy to mix up
Ask finishing option: single ring in the center, or elastic on both top and bottom
Ask fabric option: Indian regular, Turkish, or imported (most expensive)
Ask the plansifter make/model as an alternative to exact dimensions -- sizes are frame-specific and vary a lot between machines
Ask quantity of bags/pieces required
If the client has a specific fabric or the exact old sleeve, request a picture or a sample -- easy to send the wrong size without one
Ask variant: with hole or without hole
Ask material: MS (regular iron), or stainless steel if requested
Ask quantity
Ask material: mild steel (standard) or stainless steel if requested
Ask gauge: 28 gauge or 32 gauge
Ask quantity
Ask the manufacturer name of the plansifter
Ask the size of the plansifter
Ask quantity in pieces
Request pictures to confirm the exact part -- this is a large, made-to-order part, not stocked
Ask what it is for -- plansifter suspension/hanging vs general lifting/hoisting -- since the spec needed differs by use
Ask thickness/diameter of the wire rope (mm)
Ask length/quantity required
Ask material/construction: mild steel (galvanized) or stainless steel, and specific grade if the client has a preference
If unsure of the exact rope needed, offer a reference picture
Ask the make of the plansifter -- frame size is machine-specific
Ask finish: plain wooden, or with Sunmica laminate (increases service life)
Ask what sits underneath the mesh: round-hole perforated sheet (6 mm holes) or double crimped mesh, and for the perforated option ask gauge -- 28 gauge (better quality) or 32 gauge (cheaper, thinner)
Ask quantity, priced per piece
If unsure, offer/request a picture
Ask brand of the plansifter
Ask size of the plansifter
Ask section of the box (E section or other)
Ask quantity of boxes
Ask the working air pressure / compressor capacity available at the client's site
Ask the pin/staple size the tool should take (see Staple Pin)
Ask brand preference and quantity
If unsure, offer a reference picture
Ask knob type: metal or plastic in the center
Ask quantity
Ask diameter (mm) -- 16 mm is the standard/default size -- and hardness if known
Ask bounce type: high bounce or medium bounce
Ask quantity -- MOQ 500 pcs, order in multiples of 500
Ask mesh count (holes per inch); if the client does not know it, ask the opening in microns or mm (mm = wire-to-wire distance)
Ask wire thickness in mm or gauge
Ask width -- standard is 4 ft (3 ft, 5 ft, 2 m, or wider also available)
Ask length required; quantity is priced per meter
Ask grade: 304 (standard, corrosion-resistant) or 202 (cheaper, lower corrosion resistance)
Ask leg length and crown width (mm) -- must match the tacker brand/model, since pins for one gun brand do not always fit another; confirm which tacker/brand the client owns before quoting
Ask material: galvanized or stainless
Ask number of boxes required -- 1 box = 20 packets, and it is priced/sold per box
Ask trim: with brush or with studs
Ask size and quantity
Ask which trim combination the client currently has fitted: with brush, with studs, with metal knob, or with plastic knob
If the brush variant, ask quality: polyurethane, PU, or PU with a full internal nylon brush hidden inside (most expensive)
Ask size (length x width, mm) and quantity -- ordered in multiples of 100
Request a picture or the old part -- this design has the most variants in the range
